The letter reached Marcus at noon and was wet at the corners, as if the sea had tried to read it first. He opened it on an overturned barrel because the warehouse table was covered with charts and excuses. The handwriting belonged to a cautious man, yet the words hurried. That mismatch troubled him more than any open alarm would have done. It is the quiet messages that arrive with company behind them. He read once, then twice, and lifted his head toward the channel where the light lay flat and metallic. No vessel showed there. Even so, he folded the page as a sailor reefs canvas before rough weather, tucked it inside his jacket, and called for a lantern though the day had not yet begun to dim.
